text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] High tail latency and rising queue depth on runtime-pool-us-west-2 — 5xxs increasing, p95 token latency > 2s :rotating_light:

jess: saw the alert, looks like a sudden spike in long-context jobs, possibly a batch of big sequences. p50 is fine but queues are piling.

omar_oncall: jumping in — can someone post the current in-flight and queue metrics?

nick_r: from Grafana quick glance: max_in_flight=512, in_flight_active=512, queued=2.1k, shed_count=0, avg_seq_len=6.2k tokens.

maria_infra: confirmed, the routing layer sent a few thousand legacy long-run requests from a single customer region. They've been hitting our slow path and filling the scheduler.

katy: customer is @acme-analytics (managed) — flagged for potential user impact. CX ticket created.

jess: mitigation proposal: 1) immediate soft-drop for requests > 2048 tokens 2) reduce max_in_flight to 400 to free cores 3) enable fast-fail for streaming on that model variant.

omar_oncall: agree. I'll apply soft-drop rule at the edge and cut max_in_flight. Nick, can you run the commands?

nick_r: applying now — edge rule to drop >2048 sequences for model 'redwood-xt-16k' on us-west-2:

```
# traffic-control tool
trafficctl set-rate-limit --scope us-west-2 --model redwood-xt-16k --max-tokens 2048 --action soft-drop
```

nick_r: decreasing max_in_flight on runtime pool:

```
kubectl patch config runtime-pool-us-west-2 -p '{"spec":{"max_in_flight":400}}'
```

nick_r: restarting scheduler rolling restart (5s between pods)

ops-bot: rolling-restart initiated for runtime-pool-us-west-2 (pods: 12)

jess: also flipping the streaming flag off for that model in region (graceful degrade) until queues normalize. This will make calls fast-fail instead of blocking.

maria_infra: note: disabling streaming will increase token throughput on CPU for short responses, but avoids long-lived connections hogging slots.

omar_oncall: pushing changes. We'll monitor queue depth and p95. If shedding breaches >10% we may need to escalate to quota bump + additional nodes.

incident-bot: change recorded: [soft-drop, max_in_flight=400, streaming_disabled] by nick_r at 3300001125

nick_r: monitoring now — queue: 2.1k -> 1.3k in 45s, in_flight_active 400 steady, p95 dropped from 2.1s to 0.9s.

katy: reporting to CX: "We implemented emergency traffic shaping to reduce latency; some very long requests may have been dropped or failed fast — your account saw a reduced throughput window. Ops continue to monitor."

jess: next steps: 1) identify offending job patterns and ask ACME to rerun with chunking 2) consider temporary customer-specific quota cap for long-context jobs 3) plan permanent queueing rule: prioritize short jobs when queue > 1k.

omar_oncall: I'll start the ACME contact and propose a temporary policy. Also rolling a soft-scaling job to add 2 extra GPUs to the pool as fallback (will take ~7m).

nick_r: starting autoscale add:

```
scalectl add-instances --pool runtime-pool-us-west-2 --count 2 --type a100-40
```

ops-bot: scale request accepted, new instances provisioning (eta ~6m)

maria_infra: note on risk: adding instances might delay due to image pull; prefer to keep soft-drop in place until healthy.

omar_oncall: handoff incoming — I need to head to a quick meeting at 3300001165. Jess, you good to take lead?

jess: I can take it. Omar, leave notes on what to watch.

omar_oncall: notes: watch queue depth and shed_count, verify the scale completes, watch for any customer escalations. If shedding > 15% or p95 > 1.5s revert streaming enable and consider full model variant fallback (lower-context 8k quantized variant).

incident-bot: oncall-handoff: from omar_oncall to jess at 3300001168

jess: acknowledged — taking over. Monitoring shows queue at ~900, p95=0.7s, shed_count=48 (low). Scaling completed, 2 instances added.

katy: customer update sent. No active SLA breach yet, but tracking.

nick_r: logging mitigation actions to incident log with tags: runtime, queue, soft-drop, streaming-disabled, autoscale.

jess: Plan to keep soft-drop and reduced max_in_flight for 15 minutes, then slowly increase max_in_flight to 480 if metrics stable. We'll keep streaming disabled for now.

maria_infra: I'll open a follow-up to add a policy: "priority inversion" — short jobs get a priority boost once queue>800. Also suggest a per-tenant long-request quota.

katy: adding that to the roadmap ticket.

jess: closing loop: if anyone sees a secondary spike ping me. I'll update the incident thread with post-mortem notes later. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: incident actions: soft-drop enabled, max_in_flight=400, streaming_disabled, autoscale +2 nodes. Actions will be auto-archived in 24h.

incident-bot: thread closed for active mitigation at 3300001180
